heading: INT. DEPARTMENT STORE - PERFUME COUNTER - DAY

units.text: INT. DEPARTMENT STORE - PERFUME COUNTER - DAY
Glass cases.
Gilt mirrors.
A faint cloud of mixed scents hangs in the air.
MISS PRISCILLA ODUYA-FAIRBANKS, 40s, saleslady in a white smock, arranges tiny bottles with surgical precision.
Across the counter, MR. LEOPOLD KOWALCZYK-ADEBAYO, 50s, wearing a bowler hat, lifts a flask and sniffs it suspiciously.
Next to him, his wife MRS. GENEVIEVE KOWALCZYK-ADEBAYO, 40s, in a feathered hat, glares at the saleslady.
Their teenage son OSWIN, 15, hangs behind them, bored.
A floorwalker, MR. THEODORE ACHTERBERG-NWOSU, 60s, with a carnation in his lapel, hovers nearby, wringing his hands.
This smells like a wet dog.
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: That is our finest civet, sir.
units.name: PRISCILLA

units.text: Leopold, put it down.
units.name: GENEVIEVE

units.text: I like it.
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: You like everything that offends me.
units.name: GENEVIEVE

units.text: Can we go?
units.name: OSWIN

units.text: Madam, sir, perhaps the rose water--
units.name: THEODORE

units.text: No rose water!
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: ^I'll have the rose water.
units.name: GENEVIEVE

units.text: Priscilla sets two bottles on the counter.
Leopold and Genevieve both grab for the same one.
They tug.
The flask flies out of their hands, bounces off Oswin's shoulder, and crashes to the floor in a spray of glass and scent.
Everyone freezes.
A rolling fog of lavender drifts across the shop.
Smells like a wet dog.
units.name: OSWIN

units.text: Theodore faints.
Priscilla catches him.
Leopold throws his bowler hat in the air.
I'll take it!
units.name: LEOPOLD
